incidents.title: Expired UAT fixture expiry blocks ShadowBroker bootstrap
incidents.symptoms: Broker connect failed: No NIFTY PE strike 23500 for expiry 2026-06-23 in instrument master
incidents.business_impact: KAVACH and SARANSH could not load virtual positions; /register and /positions broken
incidents.trading_impact: ATO module did not start; no mock order flow
incidents.root_cause: uat/deployed_positions/positions.json retained past weekly expiry; instrument master drops expired series
contributing_factors: No auto-roll on weekly expiry boundary
incidents.fix_implemented: resolve_fixture_trading_expiry() rolls to nearest valid weekly; ShadowBroker clears virtual ledger on roll
incidents.fix_rationale: UAT book remains loadable without manual fixture edit every expiry day; stale virtual fills cannot corrupt qty
incidents.regression_risk: New weekly expiry without strikes in master may still fail — operator should refresh screenshot
remaining_risks: Operator fixture still shows 23 Jun label until new screenshot ingested
preventive_measures: Refresh Sensibull screenshot after weekly expiry
lessons_learned: UAT fixture expiry must roll or block with clear operator message
Virtual ledger must reset when core book expiry changes
future_recommendations: Optional Telegram reminder on expiry day if fixture age > 5 days

incidents.title: Mid-session WebSocket false failover — stale watchdog grace gap
incidents.symptoms: WS connected at 10:46:02 then ATO auto-paused nifty_ltp_websocket_failed at 10:46:05 before first tick
incidents.technical_impact: on_feed_stale → on_websocket_crash → REST fallback + algo pause cascade
incidents.trading_impact: ATO paused repeatedly with nifty_ltp_feed_stale warnings
incidents.root_cause: Feed stale watchdog only applied 09:15 startup grace, not grace after mid-session WS reconnect when last_update_at is None
incidents.fix_implemented: mark_transport_started() + is_within_transport_grace() — 30s grace after WS connect / REST service start
incidents.fix_rationale: Distinguishes cold reconnect from true feed death
incidents.regression_risk: Very slow first tick (>30s) could still false-positive — monitor ws_ltp audit log
lessons_learned: Transport-level grace must cover reconnect, not only market open

incidents.title: DRISHTI cold-start without JWT + ATO pause/resume churn after false WS failover
incidents.symptoms: Start All 10:43 without JWT until 10:44:52; false WS failover 10:46:05; ~25 min ATO pause/resume churn on nifty_ltp_feed_stale
incidents.root_cause: Mid-session reconnect lacked transport grace (STAB-06 fix); on_feed_stale_cleared immediately resumed on brief fresh cache while REST was flaky
incidents.fix_implemented: Transport grace on reconnect + AUTO_RESUME_STABLE_SECONDS=45 sustained can_auto_resume_feed_recovery before auto-resume
validation_performed: Post-fix session no pause/resume churn in drishti logs
lessons_learned: Never auto-resume ATO on first stale_cleared tick — require sustained trading-ready cache

incidents.title: DRISHTI cache replace race caused feed task exits and restart churn
incidents.symptoms: NIFTY feed task exited repeatedly with [WinError 5] Access is denied replacing data/nifty_ltp_cache.json, followed by watchdog restarts and KAVACH stale-cache pauses
incidents.business_impact: Operator saw repeated reconnect-style feed churn while the upstream WebSocket could still connect successfully.
incidents.technical_impact: Local cache persistence failure was misclassified as feed-task death, which triggered watchdog restarts and downstream stale-cache cascades.
incidents.trading_impact: KAVACH/ATO lost fresh cache visibility and paused on stale reads even though the transport itself was not consistently failing.
incidents.root_cause: write_nifty_ltp_cache() raised after a short Windows os.replace retry window. Transient file-lock races on nifty_ltp_cache.json therefore tore down the live feed task.
contributing_factors: Shared cache file is replaced frequently during market updates
Windows file-lock races can block rename/replace longer than the prior retry window
Feed watchdog treated any cache-write exception as a dead feed task
incidents.investigation: logs_uat/runtime/2026-06/2026-06-25/drishti/logs/all.log shows repeated WinError 5 cache-replace failures at 13:34, 13:35, and 13:39 IST with watchdog restarts after each exit.
incidents.fix_implemented: Extended Windows-safe replace retries and changed NIFTY cache writes to log-and-return on persistent replace-lock races instead of raising and killing the feed task.
incidents.fix_rationale: A transient local file lock should not be interpreted as a transport disconnect. The feed task now survives short-lived cache persistence races, reducing false restart and stale-cache cascades.
incidents.regression_risk: If another process holds the cache file lock for several seconds, cache freshness can still degrade and KAVACH may still pause; however DRISHTI no longer enters a restart storm for the same local file issue.
validation_performed: Added regression tests for transient and persistent Windows cache replace locks
Reviewed 2026-06-25 UAT logs to confirm the repeated restart pattern originated from cache replace failures
stress_testing: Repeated retry-path simulation via new cache replace lock tests
remaining_risks: Broader runtime verification remains dependent on long-running bot checks completing in this environment
preventive_measures: Keep Windows file-replace retries tuned for high-frequency cache writers
Do not let local cache persistence failures tear down the transport task
lessons_learned: Not every feed-task exception is a network problem; local filesystem races can create transport-like symptoms
Shared disk cache layers need their own resilience budget separate from WebSocket retry logic
future_recommendations: Add explicit telemetry for cache-write failure counts in DRISHTI health/status
Consider harmonizing other high-frequency JSON writers with the same Windows retry policy
